accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:cic-identification and all inferential statements
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Cyclically comonotone CiC identification is inherited from TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC rather than derived here.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The headline is conditional on the periodic-lift cyclically comonotone CiC model and its additional map-identification conditions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves pointwise CLTs for d>=3 and leaves d=2 open except P=Q=uniform on the torus; Proposition 29 gives covariance I_2/(4pi).

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v2, corresponding to the 2024 Journal of Causal Inference article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source identifies the counterfactual map under added cyclic-comonotonicity conditions and provides a consistency/rate result, not a four-sample pointwise limit law.
The paper establishes Frechet differentiability for a smooth curve of target densities with a fixed reference measure through a linearized Monge--Ampere equation.
The paper studies the point-mass influence function for transport-based quantiles and its pole singularity.
The result is for empirical Brenier potentials and normalization-invariant weighted potential contrasts, rather than pointwise map gradients.
The paper develops bootstrap consistency and an asymptotically valid confidence band for a one-dimensional transport map.

The paper identifies scalar ATT/distributional effects under a distributional bridge and develops efficient orthogonal CiC estimators with asymptotic inference; it is not a bivariate nested-Brenier pointwise-map result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add SunTchetgenTchetgen2025DebiasedCiC to related work and state a strict non-overlap: scalar orthogonal ATT/distributional inference under its distributional bridge versus fixed-grid bivariate nested Brenier-map inference under cyclic comonotonicity.
State a corollary that embeds the one-dimensional scalar CiC submodel and explicitly contrasts its root-n regular regime with the two-dimensional logarithmic pointwise regime.

Promote the nonseparable numerical kill test into a preregistered analytic boundary result: identify a checkable coefficient class for which the frozen-pole remainder is controlled, even before the full uniform theorem.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature map to incorporate and distinguish the missed CiC-inference comparator, then advance the analytically well-posed field-tier kernel to Stage 0.
